findings.F1: The book's failure is a size problem: per case over 48 hours the unusual move is +0.10 % against a 0.19 % round trip (0.5 times), so most of what the book earns is the coin's drift (+0.27 % of the +0.37 % total). It sits in a position 73 % of the bars at a mean allocation of 0.55, and it trails holding in the bull years (2020 book 0.0013 against coin 0.0042 a day, 2021 0.0011 against 0.0041, 2024 0.0007 against 0.0024). That is where its Sharpe falls short of holding's (-0.12) and where its mean daily return falls short of the bar (0.00044).
findings.F2: The rebound after an evening fall is graded by how turbulent the last 24 hours were against the last 30 days. Measured as 24-hour hourly volatility over 30-day hourly volatility, the 48-hour excess of fall evenings rises across the quintiles of this ratio: -0.62 % (t -2.49), -0.09 %, -0.12 %, +0.46 % (t 1.79), +0.67 % (t 2.38), with about 800 independent cases each.
findings.F3: Depth and turbulence together carry the idea. Deeper-than-median falls in the top turbulence tercile earn +0.95 % excess over 48 hours (t 3.42, n 800), strength 0.13, total move +1.22 %, which is 6.4 times the cost. The same deep falls in the bottom tercile lose -0.69 % (t -2.58, n 568), strength -0.10.
findings.F4: The turbulent-fall rebound mostly holds across years. In the top turbulence tercile the 48-hour excess is positive in 7 of 8 years (+0.50 % to +1.62 %), the exception being 2022 at -1.19 %. In the bottom tercile it is negative in 5 of 8 years, including 2018 at -2.08 % (t -3.56) and 2025 at -1.37 % (t -2.73). These calm-fall losses come in the bear periods that lie under the book's deepest fall (53 %, Calmar 0.18).
findings.F5: Within turbulent days, a fall spread across many hours rebounds more than one made by a single hour. With the largest hour's share of the day's total absolute move as the jump measure, high-turbulence low-jump falls earn +1.42 % excess (t 3.25, n 341, strength 0.21), while high-turbulence high-jump falls earn +0.08 % (t 0.28, n 600). Calm-day jump-made falls keep falling, at -0.91 % (t -2.89, n 319).
findings.F6: The idea's horizon is right; its move does not outlast 2 days. The fall evenings' excess is +0.22 % over 96 hours (t 0.94, n 2144) and -0.13 % over 168 hours (t -0.34, n 1158).
findings.F7: Evening falls that come while the coin is above its 30-day mean rebound and those below it do not. The excess is +0.34 % over 48 hours above the mean (t 2.02, n 1601) and -0.13 % below it (t -0.86, n 2395).

ideas.idea: The more a coin has fallen over the 24 hours up to the 20:00 UTC close, the more it rises over the next 2 days, only while its hourly volatility over those 24 hours is high against its hourly volatility over the past 30 days; the higher that ratio, the larger the rebound.
ideas.consequence: An evening long after a deep fall is worth taking when the day was unusually turbulent for the coin, and refused when the fall came on a calm day, where it tends to continue.
ideas.name: turbulent evening fall rebound

ideas.idea: The more a coin has fallen over the 24 hours up to the 20:00 UTC close, the more it rises over the next 2 days, only while that day's hourly volatility is high against the past 30 days, and the more so the more evenly the fall was spread across the 24 hours rather than made by its largest hour.
ideas.consequence: On a turbulent day a fall built across many hours is the one to buy for two days, while a fall made by one violent hour gives little rebound.
ideas.name: spread turbulent fall rebound

ideas.idea: The more a coin has fallen over the 24 hours up to the 20:00 UTC close, the more it rises over the next 2 days, only while its close is above its 30-day mean price.
ideas.consequence: An evening dip inside a coin's monthly uptrend is worth buying for two days, while one below the monthly mean is not.
ideas.name: evening dip in uptrend
